summary.title: SYSTEMS OF HECKE EIGENVALUES ON SUBSCHEMES OF SHIMURA VARIETIES
summary.executive_summary: This paper establishes that the systems of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in the coherent cohomology of any mod p abelian type compact Shimura variety at hyperspecial level are identical to those appearing in any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme. The author generalizes previous results by Goldring-Koskivirta and Terakado-Yu, which were limited to smooth, zero-dimensional subschemes, to include higher-dimensional and possibly singular subschemes. The central result, Theorem A, proves that for a compact abelian type Shimura variety $S_K$ and any prime-to-p Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme $Y_K$, the systems of Hecke eigenvalues in the direct sum of cohomology groups $H^0(S_K, V(\eta))$ and $H^0(Y_K, V(\eta))$ are the same. The proof overcomes two main technical obstacles: the absence of nowhere vanishing Hecke-invariant sections on singular subschemes and the failure of the conormal sequence to be exact or consist of locally free sheaves. The author introduces a "going-down" argument that intersects the subscheme with the smallest length stratum it meets and successively removes nonsingular points to obtain a smooth, closed subscheme $Z_K$ admitting a nowhere vanishing Hecke-equivariant section. By relating eigenvalues on $Y_K$ and $S_K$ to those on $Z_K$, the author proves the equivalence. The paper also extends these results to noncompact Shimura varieties and nonclosed subschemes, such as Ekedahl-Oort strata, length strata, and central leaves, under specific conditions regarding properness and closure. These findings unify the spectral properties of Hecke actions across various geometric strata of Shimura varieties, providing a robust framework for understanding the arithmetic geometry of these spaces.

claims.description: Systems of Hecke eigenvalues on any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme are the same as those on the Shimura variety.
The equivalence holds for nonclosed subschemes like Ekedahl-Oort strata and central leaves under certain conditions.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper establishes that the systems of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in the coherent cohomology of any mod p abelian type compact Shimura variety at hyperspecial level are identical to those appearing in any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme. The author generalizes previous results by Goldring-Koskivirta and Terakado-Yu, which were limited to smooth, zero-dimensional subschemes, to include higher-dimensional and possibly singular subschemes. The central result, Theorem A, proves that for a compact abelian type Shimura variety $S_K$ and any prime-to-p Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme $Y_K$, the systems of Hecke eigenvalues in the direct sum of cohomology groups $H^0(S_K, V(\eta))$ and $H^0(Y_K, V(\eta))$ are the same. The proof overcomes two main technical obstacles: the absence of nowhere vanishing Hecke-invariant sections on singular subschemes and the failure of the conormal sequence to be exact or consist of locally free sheaves. The author introduces a "going-down" argument that intersects the subscheme with the smallest length stratum it meets and successively removes nonsingular points to obtain a smooth, closed subscheme $Z_K$ admitting a nowhere vanishing Hecke-equivariant section. By relating eigenvalues on $Y_K$ and $S_K$ to those on $Z_K$, the author proves the equivalence. The paper also extends these results to noncompact Shimura varieties and nonclosed subschemes, such as Ekedahl-Oort strata, length strata, and central leaves, under specific conditions regarding properness and closure. These findings unify the spectral properties of Hecke actions across various geometric strata of Shimura varieties, providing a robust framework for understanding the arithmetic geometry of these spaces.

Research Context
The mod p fiber of an abelian type Shimura variety has a prime-to-p Hecke algebra action. Subschemes like Ekedahl-Oort strata and central leaves are invariant under this action. Serre showed eigenvalues on modular curves match those on the supersingular locus. Goldring-Koskivirta generalized this to Hodge-type Shimura varieties and zero-dimensional strata. Terakado-Yu extended the method to central leaves in the basic Newton stratum. Previous works focused on smooth subschemes of dimension 0. This paper addresses higher dimensional and possibly singular subschemes.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is whether Hecke eigenvalues on subschemes match those on the whole variety. The hypothesis is that systems of Hecke eigenvalues are the same for any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme. The author predicts this holds for higher-dimensional and singular subschemes. The study aims to prove analogous results for noncompact varieties and nonclosed subschemes. Specific attention is given to Ekedahl-Oort strata, length strata, and central leaves. The goal is to establish equivalence of eigenvalue systems across these geometric structures.

Methodological Details
The study considers Shimura varieties of abelian type at hyperspecial level K. The group G is assumed to be equal to its cuspidal quotient Gc. A prime p not equal to 2 is fixed where G is unramified. The special fiber $S_K$ of the Kisin-Vasiu integral model is used. Automorphic line bundles $V(\eta)$ are associated to L-dominant characters. The Hecke action is defined via push-pull operations on coherent sheaves. The theory of G-zips is used to define strata and Hasse invariants. Ekedahl-Oort and length strata are defined via the Weyl group and length function. Hasse invariants are sections whose nonvanishing loci define the strata. Central leaves are defined via isomorphisms of Dieudonné modules.

Procedures And Architectures
The proof uses a going-down argument to relate eigenvalues on the variety to subschemes. A further going-down argument intersects $Y_K$ with the smallest length stratum. Nonsingular points are successively removed to obtain a smooth subscheme $Z_K$. The subscheme $Z_K$ admits a nowhere vanishing Hecke-equivariant section. The conormal exact sequence is modified to relate eigenvalues on $Y_K$ and $S_K$ to $Z_K$. Serre vanishing is used to ensure surjectivity of cohomology maps. The going-up argument applies verbatim to relate eigenvalues on $Z_K$ to $Y_K$ and $S_K$. For noncompact cases, toroidal compactifications are used. The Hecke action extends to the compactification $S^\Sigma_K$.

Key Results
Theorem A states that for compact abelian type Shimura varieties, eigenvalue systems are the same for any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme. Theorem B extends this to Ekedahl-Oort strata, length strata, and central leaves. If $S_K$ is proper and $C_K$ is closed in its Ekedahl-Oort stratum, eigenvalues match. The proof relies on the existence of Hasse invariants for the going-down argument. Lemma 3.2.2 shows that if $Z_K$ is proper and smooth with an injective section, eigenvalues on $Y_K$ appear in $Z_K$. Lemma 3.2.4 shows the reverse implication for proper $Y_K$ and closed $Z_K$. Theorem 3.3.2 provides results for locally closed subschemes and noncompact varieties. If $Y_K$ meets the basic locus, eigenvalue systems are equivalent.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The results unify the spectral properties of Hecke actions across different geometric strata. The method overcomes technical issues with singular and higher-dimensional subschemes. The use of length strata and Hasse invariants is crucial for the proof. The findings extend the understanding of Hecke eigenvalues beyond zero-dimensional cases. The equivalence of eigenvalues suggests a deep connection between the global and local geometry.

Contradictions And Limitations
The theory of toroidal compactifications for abelian type Shimura varieties is not fully developed. The assumption $G = G_c$ is technical and may limit generality. Results for noncompact varieties require the variety to be of Hodge type. The proof relies on the existence of specific Hasse invariants.

Claims
Systems of Hecke eigenvalues on any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme are the same as those on the Shimura variety. Theorem A explicitly states this equivalence for compact abelian type varieties. The proof constructs a smooth subscheme $Z_K$ with matching eigenvalues. The result is limited to hyperspecial level and abelian type. This allows transferring spectral information between the variety and its strata.
The equivalence holds for nonclosed subschemes like Ekedahl-Oort strata and central leaves under certain conditions. Theorem B covers Ekedahl-Oort strata and length strata. Central leaves in the basic Newton stratum are included. Properness or closure conditions are required for some cases. This extends the applicability of the result to important geometric structures.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The proof uses a stepwise removal of nonsingular points to ensure smoothness. Serre vanishing is used to handle cohomology surjectivity. The conormal sequence is modified to handle non-locally free sheaves.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is proving Hecke eigenvalue equivalence for any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme. 2. The strongest evidence is the construction of a smooth subscheme $Z_K$ with matching eigenvalues. 3. The future path involves extending these results to more general Shimura varieties and levels.
